Reading the target menu

The target menu is the board at the stand that tells the shooter what is coming: which traps, in what order, and what kind of doubles.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the menu lists the traps in shooting order and must name any special targets: 90 mm, 70 mm or 60 mm, battue or rabbit. Referees check beforehand that the traps match the menu. A layout gives 25 targets: 15 singles and 5 doubles. The doubles may only use targets already shown as singles from the same stand, and the squad shoots the singles first.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 2 · Target menu at the stand

Each double is marked with its type. On report: the second target leaves on the sound of the first shot. Simultaneous: both targets leave together. Rafale: two targets from the same trap, one after the other, in Sporting™ only. Menus look different from ground to ground, so read the words, not just the letters.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Tip: Example: on a line of 4 stands, one stand has only 3 traps, and 3 singles and 2 doubles are shot there. Its menu might read: singles A, B, C, then a simultaneous double A + B and a rafale C + C (the letters are traps). On this stand at least one double must be simultaneous or rafale: two doubles on report are not allowed (Chapter 2 · Doubles at a position with 3 machines).

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 2 · Doubles at a position with 3 machines

Compak® Sporting

In Compak® Sporting a menu is posted at each of the five stations. Each station has five targets, in one of three mixes: five singles; three singles and one double; or one single and two doubles. The singles may come from the traps in any order. All five stations have the same kind of double, and the stations are linked in a chain: the first target of each double is the last target shot at the previous station. For competitions FITASC offers 40 ready-made setting tables (plans of which traps are shot at each station).

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 17 · The menu card at each station

Compak® Sporting

Tip: Before stepping onto a Compak® Sporting station, many shooters say its menu quietly to themselves: “A, then F, then B, then C and E on report.” This can help them remember the order.

Key points

  • Read the menu before you step up: trap order, special targets, type of each double.
  • Sporting™ menu: traps in order plus special targets (90 mm, 70 mm or 60 mm, battue or rabbit).
  • A Sporting™ layout gives 25 targets: 15 singles and 5 doubles; doubles use targets already shown as singles; singles first.
  • Doubles: on report, simultaneous, rafale (Sporting™ only).
  • Compak® Sporting: five targets per station, same double type on all stations, each double starts with the previous station's last target.
Stand Talk

  • Coach Read the menu: on station three you have A, then F, then B, then the pair C and E on report.

    Meaning: Station 3: three singles, then a double on report; five targets in all.

  • Coach Same traps, new menu — don't shoot from memory.

    Meaning: The order has changed since the last round.

  • Coach Three singles, then a simo pair.

    Meaning: 'Simo' is short for a simultaneous double.

For the interpreter
  • Shooters really say “menu”, so keep the word when you translate.
  • Before your shooter steps up, read the menu aloud to them in their language, letter by letter: 'A, then F, then B, then the pair C and E on report.'

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Which special targets must a Sporting™ menu show?

    1. Only the colours of the targets
    2. 90 mm, 70 mm, 60 mm, battue or rabbit
    3. Only rabbits and battues
    4. None; the referee announces them
    Answer

    90 mm, 70 mm, 60 mm, battue or rabbit

    The menu must list the traps in order and any special target types.

  2. In Compak® Sporting, with which target does each double start?

    1. Always the target from trap A
    2. A new target that was not shown before
    3. The last target shot at the previous station
    4. Any target the shooter chooses first
    Answer

    The last target shot at the previous station

    The doubles chain across stations: each begins with the last target of the station before.

  3. Which type of double exists only in Sporting™?

    1. Rafale
    2. On report
    3. Simultaneous
    4. None
    Answer

    Rafale

    Compak® Sporting doubles are on report or simultaneous; rafale is a Sporting™ double.
